The stop is a round-1 review escalation with cause `decision`, round 1, no refusal named. Its one decision finding, F10, asks whether this run may delete internal/treadleengine, its stencils and its roles (D8). Neither the board entry nor the decision record settles that.
On the board entry, the 2026-11-18 operator decision names treadle among the modules to build on. The 2026-10-16 operator decision keeps the treadle judge stencils for Hardener, to be re-derived from the Bouncer judge when Hardener is built, "so no dead-code sweep removes them". The draft also says treadleengine's retirement "is a separate call, made once Tenter lands". The entry's Done-when names deleting crucible/, not treadle.
D8 deletes treadle on dead-code grounds (no consumer, reached from no main). D3 builds Hardener on the Bouncer instead of treadle, and support-log Q1 shows that was an auto-pick, not an operator answer. Q13 shows the writer left the deletion for the parent to overrule.
A yes would widen the task's scope beyond Done-when into a call the board reserves as separate, so I may not settle it that way. A no would also leave a choice open: whether this run re-derives the kept stencils, which the 2026-10-16 note expects when Hardener is built but which nothing in this design would use. So the question goes to the operator.
The one part of F10 the board does settle is that D8's rationale misquotes the 2026-10-16 note ("only until Hardener is built"). I recorded the exact replacement as an arbiter decision.
The round's BLOCKING findings F1, F2 and F3 are not decision findings. The committed record after round 1's fix already carries their fixes: D8 has the agentconfig premise and reinterpretation, D4 runs gate keys through --gate, and D5 routes the reaps through runproc.End with a PATTERN-child-processes change. A continue would put those fixes before fresh reviewers.
